text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 page - KV cache mem growth + continuous-batching perf cliff detected (auto-alert). Affected: /v1/generate (redwood-gen-v1), sustained latency spikes + OOM risk. Root signature: speculative-decoding interleaving with long-prefix KV cache -> cache divergence and unbounded prefix growth. First saw spike 2025-11-06T14:12:01Z. Paging oncall.

maria: oncall ack - looking. @aj can you pull logs for batcher and kvcache? I'll check perf graphs / flame.

aj: on it. quick summary from the alert: 24% p95 latency increase, mem from 45%->95% on the batcher hosts over ~20m, batch queue depth jumped x3. Logs show repeated speculative-decode fallback paths creating new KV entries per draft run. snippet from batcher logs:

```
batcher: enqueue req id=abc123 len=2048 spec_mode=on
spec-decode: created kv-prefix k:rdw:genv1:abc123:draft:0..n
kvcache: insert prefix size=6MB
kvcache: insert prefix size=7MB
```

That pattern repeated per token when speculative decoding triggered, causing many tiny prefixes instead of shared prefix reuse.

tyler: omg, saw similar earlier on canary when we tried aggressive speculative for latency reduction. thought cache compaction would handle it, but compaction is async and can't keep up with continuous batches at high QPS.

sylvie: hypothesis: speculative-decoding writes new prefix keys for each speculative branch because draft/target sync hasn't deduped k-prefix IDs. Also continuous-batching groups requests that don't share prefixes, so KV entry count explodes. Mitigation options: 1) disable speculative decoding flag for redwood-gen-v1 (fastest), 2) lower batcher max_batch_size and max_wait to limit transient queue depth, 3) mass invalidate newly created prefixes older than Xs.

maria: agreed. priority is stabilize latency and memory. Plan: flip spec-decoding off for prod model, then reduce batch size from 64->8 on the batcher pool, then run prefix invalidation sweep. I'll execute 1 and 2 now. tagging @ops-bot to roll config.

ops-bot: received. beginning rolling config change across batcher-pool-prod (10 nodes). 1) toggling feature flag spec_decode.enabled=false -> targeting rollout 30s/node. 2) applying batcher config patch: max_batch_size: 8, max_wait_ms: 30. rolling.

aj: pushing a quick hotfix script to gate the cache writer on speculative mode, adding defensive check to avoid creating more than N prefixes per request. patch link: https://git.internal/redwood/batcher/commit/fe34a2 (deploy is queued if needed). If toggle works, we can skip hotfix deploy for now.

maria: ops-bot reports first 3 nodes done, mem usage leveling on those. metrics: host-3 mem 92% -> 62% after toggle. p95 latency dropping. keeping watch.

chantal: CS update: ACME-prod saw latency spikes and intermittent 5xxs starting ~14:10. They've already opened a ticket. I'm drafting a status page blurb and will tell them we're mitigating and have reduced their error rate - will update in 30m. :+1:

tyler: re: cache invalidation approach - prefer selective invalidation: remove prefixes matching pattern `k:rdw:genv1:*:draft:*` older than 15s to avoid nuking warm shared prefixes. command we can run on redis cluster (careful):

```
# dry-run, list keys
redis-cli -c -h redis-prod 'SCAN 0 MATCH "k:rdw:genv1:*:draft:*" COUNT 1000'

# delete by eval to avoid mass blocking
redis-cli -c -h redis-prod EVAL "local ks=redis.call('SCAN',ARGV[1],'MATCH',ARGV[2],'COUNT',1000); for i,k in ipairs(ks) do if k~=false then redis.call('DEL',k) end end" 0 0 "k:rdw:genv1:*:draft:*"
```

sylvie: I'll run invalidation but will throttle deletes and monitor hit-rate. Also we should patch the dedupe layer so speculative drafts reuse canonical prefix when same target/draft overlaps - filing a follow-up ticket.

maria: spec decode flag toggled to OFF cluster-wide at 14:20:12Z. batcher config reduced at 14:21:05Z. metrics: p95 trending back to baseline, mem stabilized. continuing invalidation sweep now (14:30->14:36). ops-bot, confirm sweep progress?

ops-bot: sweep started, 120k keys queued, deleting in 5k batches with 5s sleep between batches. estimated finish 14:55.

aj: noticed a regression in some long-context requests after the toggle - outputs are slightly different (expected since spec was doing different sampling). No customer-facing correctness regressions flagged so far, but QA running quick eval set.

chantal: CS - ACME reports latency improved and errors dropping. Will hold off sending broader email until we confirm full stability. They requested note that some outputs may change briefly; advising to monitor.

tyler: FYI, telemetry shows prefix insertion rate back down to baseline after invalidation started. nice.

sylvie: follow-ups captured: (1) add dedupe for speculative prefix creation, (2) add backpressure/guard limiting prefix creations per req, (3) backfill compaction improvements. I'll own the dedupe ticket and aim for PR in 2 weeks.

maria: handoff to @sylvie for overnight watch. I'll update incident doc + timeline. Expected next steps: monitor batcher mem for 3h, validate no unexplained re-growth, prepare rollback plan to re-enable spec-decode with dedupe when fixed.

sylvie: taking handoff. I have dashboard links and runbook. ping me if you see mem >80% or batch queue depth >2x baseline. will update status page after sweep completes.

cs-bot: status-page updated: "Investigating: elevated latencies on /v1/generate due to internal cache growth. Mitigation in progress (feature toggle + batching config)."

maria: thanks team. postmortem template assigned to silvie (typo:sylvie). tagging for postmortem: triage timeline, root cause (spec-decoded drafts creating many unique kv prefixes + continuous batching mixing non-shared prefixes), mitigation (flag off, batch size reduction, selective invalidation), long-term fixes.

incident-bot: SEV2 -> resolved (mitigated) at 2025-11-06T15:12:01Z. follow-up: postmortem and customer outreach.

sylvie: quick note: will snapshot affected KV keys before full GC for forensic analysis (keeping one snapshot per node).
